output:
To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Handover for Thursday, for Inês (draft)

Inês,

I'm writing this at the station, so forgive the order of it. My father is ill and I am with my family. I'm on the train to the Netherlands tonight and I don't know yet how long I'll be gone. That means Thursday is yours, and I'm sorry to hand it to you like this, with a correction still open. None of it is your fault and all of it is fixable. More on both below.

First, the thing that actually matters: I trust you completely. You know this paper as well as I do. You ran the annex B sensitivity runs yourself, you know where the numbers come from and where they don't hold. If I could choose anyone to stand in front of Lindqvist and Kessler on Thursday, it would be you, and I'm not saying that to be kind. I've seen you do it. In Lisbon, when the projector died in the middle of my panel, you had the room back in about ninety seconds and nobody there thought for a second that anything had gone wrong. You are better live than you think you are. Please remember that at 12:30 on Thursday.

Now the work, in the order I'd do it.

1. The press release. This is the urgent one, so do it first thing tomorrow.
The embargoed release Hanna sent to 34 contacts on Friday says EUR 2.1 billion. It should say EUR 1.4 billion. The embargo lifts Thursday at 10:00, and a corrected version needs to be with the same list before then. Earlier is better. Talk to Hanna first thing. She'll know how to handle the re-send and how to word it with the journalists. If she needs a senior name on a corrected version, Geert knows I'm away and can sign it off. Don't wait for me on this one.

2. Slides. Deck v4, slides 6 and 9.
The 2.1 appears on both, and possibly in the speaker notes on 9, so check those too. The PDF is already corrected: v7 on the drive, pages 3, 14 and 15. Make sure that's the version that gets printed and circulated, and check with Tomás's office that they're printing v7 and not an earlier file. Anything sent out or handed round on Thursday should be v7.

Be clear with yourself about what changed: the conclusion of the paper does not change, the headline number does. The 2030 LDC-relevant revenue estimate in the old run didn't apply the free allocation phase-out. The correct figure is 1.4 billion. The summary and anything else quoting the old number needs to match. If anyone asks how it happened, it's my mistake, not yours. Say that plainly. You didn't miss anything. I found it on Monday afternoon and left you to clean it up.

3. Tomás and the logistics.
Tomás emailed on Monday with changes. The presentation is 15 minutes instead of 20, the panel starts at 12:50, and Lindqvist has to leave at 13:30. She wants to take at least two questions herself before she goes, so build that into the run of show. The version in the folder is now out of date on timings, so redo it around his email rather than trying to patch it.

Badge names from our side have to be with Tomás by Wednesday 12:00. That's a hard deadline, security won't let anyone in after it. Check who's coming from our side, including anyone you're bringing, and send the list. Abena's remote link is in the calendar invite. She tested it last week and it works.

4. Press calls, Wednesday 14:00 and 15:00.
Hanna told two journalists I'd be available Wednesday afternoon. You'll need to take them or move them, your call, you know the paper. If you take them, 1.4 is the line, and the correction is much better volunteered than discovered. Twenty minutes each, phone.

5. Kessler.
He'll come at you on the 80% pass-through in section 4. It's what they put in writing and he'll want the panel to be about that. Don't let him set the tone. The answer is in my reply note in the folder and it's a good one: 80% is the central case, annex B runs 40% and 60%, the result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%, and we say so openly. Don't get defensive, just put the sensitivity on the table. It's a stronger position than his. If he pushes on resource shuffling, we agree it's a risk, it's in section 5.2, and we recommend the Commission's monitoring report. Abena will probably back you on the LDC side. She was strong on the call.

6. Afterwards.
Lucy Tran from Halvorsen will be there with a colleague. They need two photos from the event and the attendance numbers for their grant report by 4 December. Ask Tomás for the count on the day and get someone to take proper photos, not phone snaps from the back.

If you only do three things before Thursday: the corrected release to Hanna, slides 6 and 9 plus checking that v7 is what's being printed, and the badge list to Tomás by Wednesday noon. Everything else can wobble.

That's everything I can think of. The folder is a mess but it's all in there, and everything that matters from my inbox is either in the folder or in this note. If something's missing, call me. You can call any time, but after 9 tomorrow morning I might not pick up, so try before then if it's urgent.

I'm sorry to leave you with this. It's not how I wanted the week to go and it's not what you signed up for. But if anyone can carry it, it's you.

Marieke
